notes:
# The meeting is transcribed as it is spoken {doc}
Words appear while the meeting runs, in a panel that can sit over Zoom or
fold down to a bar, and the finished transcript is beside the recording to
read, copy or search. Each line is marked with whose voice it was -- your
own microphone against what the meeting carried -- and the transcript keeps
running when the panel is closed, which is what closing it now says.

# A recording could vanish from the list {danger}
The file was on the disk and the app showed nothing: a panel saving one
setting wrote the whole document as it had loaded it minutes earlier, over
the top of what the recorder had filed in between. One setting at a time
now, re-read and written back -- and the same fault was in eight other
places, including saving a meeting and moving one to a folder. A 7 minute
25 second recording that had already been lost this way is back on its
meeting.

# The transcript no longer stops in the middle of a meeting {danger}
It stopped three minutes into one and gave no sign: the panel kept showing a
level, the status kept ticking over, and 220 seconds of speech were thrown
away while the model sat idle. Two threads were sharing the microphone
history and one of them raised, which killed the thread that runs the model
-- into a stderr pointed at /dev/null. That history is shared properly now,
one bad utterance costs one utterance rather than the meeting, the model is
started again if it ever stops anyway, and the panel says the transcript hit
a problem rather than blaming the Mac.

# One broken frame no longer ends the transcript {mic}
Under load the capture abandons the frame it was part-way through writing,
and the reader walks forward to the next one. It was walking PAST it: the
four bytes that mark a frame were eaten on the way, so the next header was
read from inside the frame behind it, which sent it looking again -- for the
rest of the meeting. Nothing raised, nothing was logged, the audio kept
being read at exactly the speed it arrived, and the panel just stopped
showing anything. On twenty-one frames with one break in them, two were
read; twenty are now.

# Every way of starting a recording asks about the room {shield}
The question about the people in the meeting was wired to one path: arming a
schedule. So the two buttons somebody actually presses while sitting in a
call -- Record now, and Record this meeting from the banner or the panel
over Zoom -- asked whether to include their microphone and never whether
anybody had been told. It is asked on all of them now, before the recorder
starts, and still only when nothing else is going to announce it.

# A meeting being recorded has a page about the recording {camcorder}
It had one only if the meeting had recorded before. A scheduled meeting
running for the first time showed the edit form instead -- so the moment
there was most to say about a meeting was the moment it looked like a blank
new-meeting page, with a line of status along the bottom of the window as
the only sign anything was happening. It now shows the run: what it is
doing, what is being said as it is said, whether the meeting was told, and
the schedule it ran under. It also carries the two things the form used to
hold while a meeting ran: whether your voice is going into this recording --
settled when the capture opened, so it is stated rather than offered -- and
the meeting notes, as the same tile the form has, saved as it is touched
because there is no Save button on this page. Edit details is gone while a
run is going: everything it could change describes a capture that is already
open, so it led to a form with every field greyed out.

# The speech model arrives by itself {download}
Transcription cannot happen at all without it, and nothing fetched it: a
fresh install had a switch that worked and a transcript that never came,
with the download buried in Settings. It is now fetched in the background
the moment somebody asks for transcripts -- the switch in Settings, or
choosing one for a meeting on the form, before the meeting is even saved --
which is the same moment the microphone switch asks macOS for permission,
and for the same reason: at the recording there is nobody in the room to
answer for it.

Not on a first launch: it is half a gigabyte and transcripts are off until
somebody turns them on. Not during a capture either -- it is the same
connection the meeting is on. A failure says nothing and is tried again;
Settings shows how far it has got if you want to watch.

# Every recording gets a folder of its own {folder}
The video, the transcript's several files, the captions and the handouts a
webinar offered all belong to one occasion, and they sat loose beside every
other occasion's: a hundred and eighty entries in one Finder window, three
quarters of them sidecars, with no way to see what belonged to what. A run
now has a directory named after itself, inside the meeting's folder, and an
interrupted capture's second part lands in it beside the first.

Recordings made before this are moved into folders of their own the next
time the app runs, quietly -- they keep their names, and the app reads both
layouts either way, so nothing depends on it having happened. Never while a
recording is under way: the recorder is writing to one of those paths. All
or nothing per run, and files the app has no record of are left alone.

# Meetings can be dragged into a folder {folder}
Up from the list into the folder rows above it, and the row under the
cursor lights up so it is clear which one will get it. A folder takes it,
Unfiled takes it back out, and Upcoming and Done refuse -- they are states a
meeting is in, not places to put it. Dropping between two rows does nothing
either: there is no order here to insert into. Several at once if several
are selected, and holding a drag over a collapsed Folders header opens it.

EVERYTHING GOES WITH IT. A folder is a directory, so a meeting that moves
takes its files -- and a recording is never one file: the transcript's
several, the captions, and the folder of handouts a webinar offered were all
being left behind, by the drag AND by renaming a meeting, which is older
than the drag. They are found by the name they share with the recording,
so anything written beside one in future comes along without being listed
anywhere.

All-or-nothing, as the rename has always been: if one file of a run cannot
go, none of them do and the meeting stays where it was, because a run with
its parts in two folders is two half recordings. Files recorded under
another name stay put and are reported rather than guessed at.

And every way of moving a meeting does this now, not just the drag:
Select-and-move, and saving the form with a different folder on it -- that
one wrote the field and left every file where it was.

# Stopping the transcript asks first, in the panel itself {mic}
Stop ends the listening for good and what is said after it cannot be
recovered from the recording, so it asks -- on a bar that slides out from
under the panel, with the words it is about to stop still readable above it.
It says the recording itself carries on. Close says the opposite, that the
transcript keeps being written, once, and then trusts you. Neither one is a
dialog any more: opening a window runs a modal, running a modal brings the
app forward over the meeting, and the question ended up in the middle of a
window nobody was looking at.

# Setting up Telegram alerts is three steps {envelope}
A button to BotFather for the token, a button to the bot that reads back
your chat id, and each one checked against Telegram as it is pasted -- so a
typo is found on the page rather than by an alert that never arrives.

---

Everything else in this release, roughly in that order:

- The transcript no longer stops twenty seconds in. The capture helper
  stopped copying audio out the first time the listener fell behind and
  never resumed: 23 seconds written and 197 dropped became 889 written and
  none dropped on the same length of meeting.
- The page stops claiming to be live once the capture is over. The recorder
  stays alive for up to forty minutes reading the recording, and everything
  that tested "is it recording" carried on as though the meeting were still
  happening -- the live transcript, the card of things still to decide, the
  bar offering to stop a recording that had finished, and an analysis card
  offering to start a second reading of the same file.
- Somebody already sharing their screen is in a meeting: the in-meeting
  panel and the offer to record missed them entirely, because sharing
  replaces the window the app was looking for.
- Closing the window quits the app, unless a recording is running -- and
  then the Dock icon brings the window back, which is what the dialog says.
- A recording notice that did not go out says so, on the run while the
  meeting is still in front of you and on the file afterwards. All three
  ways it can fail were a line in a log nobody opens.
- And when the Mac really is too busy to keep up, it says that rather than
  "catching up", which reads as a queue that will be worked through. It
  goes back to Listening by itself once nothing more is being lost.
- The live transcript opens at the top of the screen, in the middle of it,
  on the screen the meeting is on -- it opened in the bottom left corner.
  Wherever you drag it to is remembered, and now only if you dragged it.
- It is the same transcript everywhere: the page drew its lines without a
  speaker at all while the panel over Zoom said YOU on every line. Same
  line now, and the panel on the page has a ceiling and scrolls inside
  itself rather than growing until the cards below it are off the screen.
- The question for the notes saves itself a moment after the typing stops,
  the line under it says so, and a rebuild of the page landing in that
  moment writes what was typed instead of taking it away.
- Stop says so the moment it is pressed: "Stopping -- saving what it has",
  and it cannot be pressed twice.
- The transcript card has a way to READ it: View transcript opens the
  player, where the lines sit beside the video and a line can be clicked
  to jump to the moment it was said.
- The transcript's status is said in colour when it matters: stopped in the
  warning colour, a Mac that cannot keep up in the danger one, everything
  ordinary left grey.
- Automatic software updates stayed on the way it was left.
- The window resizes down again. A still at 960 pixels had put a
  2247-point floor under it.
- Clicking a paragraph of the notes no longer flattens it.
- Cards say their sentence under the title rather than under the icon.
- The recorded transcript is not repeated under the recording card, since
  the player shows it beside the video.
- The toolbar, the tab strip and the sidebar: one scale, a sliding
  selection, a count capsule that can be seen in the light, and no stray
  band behind the list.
- Encoder tuning can be edited once Custom is chosen.
